note: zizmor 1.26.1, offline, against the committed 3-workflow fixture. Numbers are re-verified on 2026-08-05 and match the 2026-06-27 regular-persona run exactly. Deterministic: a pinned version + fixed fixture + --offline yields the same output on any machine.

metrics.label: Findings on the fixture (default 'regular' persona, offline)
Same fixture, escalating persona (signal/noise tradeoff)
metrics.note: regular reproduces exactly; pedantic/auditor drift by 1-2 because the reconstructed fixture is not byte-identical to the deleted original. The durable claim is the monotonic escalation, not the exact higher-persona count.

findings.detail: 7 unpinned-uses (High/High), 2 artipacked (Medium/Low), 2 template-injection (High/High), 1 excessive-permissions (Medium/Medium), 1 dangerous-triggers (High/Medium), 1 unsound-ternary (Low/High), 1 typosquat-uses (High/Low). Severity split High 11 / Medium 3 / Low 1.

typosquat-uses catches `actons/setup-python` (one letter dropped from `actions`); unsound-ternary catches `github.ref_type == 'tag' && '' || 'staging'` where the empty-string branch is falsy, so the expression ALWAYS falls through to 'staging'.
`--offline` needs no network, no GitHub token, no Docker. The regular-persona result is deterministic for a pinned version + fixed input.

findings.claim: Non-zero exit on findings — CI gate ready.
findings.detail: Findings present -> exit 14. A clean workflow -> exit 0.

On ci-deploy.yml: 3 fixes — template-injection rewritten to env indirection (`${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}` -> env GITHUB_EVENT_PULL_REQUEST_TITLE + `${GITHUB_EVENT_PULL_REQUEST_TITLE}` in run), artipacked gets `persist-credentials: false` inserted. On release.yml: 1 fix. Applied to 2 files total.

limits.note: 7/15 findings are unpinned-uses, a blanket policy that flags even trusted actions pinned by tag (@v4). Not a false positive — a policy choice. Turn it down if you pin by tag deliberately.
Some audits (e.g. ref-confusion) only fully work in online mode (GitHub API). Offline runs use the baked-in corpus only.
Static analysis: it sees workflow STRUCTURE risk, not runtime behavior or secret values.
typosquat-uses matches against a baked-in list of popular actions; a typo of an obscure action may not be caught.
